create.name: Mary Beth LaRue
create.bio:
Mary Beth LaRue, known to students as MB, has taught yoga for more than twenty years and now works as a slow flow teacher and somatic practitioner under the name Embodied by MB. She first stepped onto a mat at twenty, looking for a way to live in her body rather than in her head, and went on to train in yoga with teachers such as Ally Hamilton, Kia Miller, Chad Dennis and Schuyler Grant, later studying somatic approaches with Britt Piper, Scott Lyons and others. She has led classes at Kripalu, 1440 Multiversity and Wanderlust, mentored newer teachers and appeared on the cover of Yoga Journal.

Her classes are unhurried, creative flows set to carefully chosen music, with room for breath, stillness and noticing sensation; the emphasis is on presence rather than performance. From her home in the Colorado mountains she teaches live weekly classes and keeps an on-demand library through her online membership, works with people one to one and in small groups, and leads retreats in person. Free practices are on her YouTube channel, and on Commune she teaches the slow flow half of The Wellest Challenge with trainer Jacy Cunningham. She also writes a Substack called Right Now It's Like This.

courses.title: Embodied Membership: virtual slow flow classes
courses.description: Her online studio, with live slow flow and meditative classes each week and an on-demand library of several hundred recorded practices. Classes are creative, music-led and paced to leave space for breath and attention.

courses.title: The Wellest Challenge
courses.description: A ten-day Commune programme that alternates short high-intensity workouts led by trainer Jacy Cunningham with slow flow yoga classes taught by Mary Beth. Designed to balance effort and ease in under twenty minutes a day.

sprint.tier_evidence: Instagram @marybethlarue 35K (og:description, 31 Oct 2026); YouTube @marybethlarue4158 1.3K (channel header row, 31 Oct 2026); no Facebook, X or TikTok linked from her site → ~36k total → local_hero
flags: Her current work leans strongly towards somatic 'nervous system' sessions for women alongside yoga; she says it is not therapy and she is not presented as a therapist, so kept as a yoga teacher, but a human should confirm she is not mainly therapy under the brief.
The Wellest Challenge is co-taught with HIIT trainer Jacy Cunningham (half fitness, half slow flow yoga); her other Commune course, The Release, is membership-only with no course page.
Membership price is not shown on her site (the page is mostly embedded Instagram reels; og:description describes the Embodied Membership), so 'Contact for pricing'.
Studied with Schuyler Grant (rank 1); no duplicate, just a link between teachers.
YouTube videos are 2–10 years old with modest views; titles had the trailing '| Embodied by MB' brand removed.
Lives in the Colorado mountains (her About page); no studio named, so availability worldwide.
left_out: 1-on-1 Somatic Work sessions ($180 USD single and packages): the page lists recovery, grief and perimenopause among reasons to come, condition-framed.

The Embodied Return ($599 USD, six-week somatic immersion): built around nervous-system regulation and protective patterns; borderline therapy framing, left out under the 'when borderline, leave out' rule.
The Release (Commune): membership-only, no course page.
Retreats: mentioned on her site but no retreat page or dates found.
'Meet Our Son' video (personal, under 2 minutes) and short meditations under ~5 minutes not prioritised.
Substack 'Right Now It's Like This': writing, not a practice/download resource; mentioned in bio only.
